messages:
aj: Heads-up — noticed a regression in tail p99 on h100 for seq=128 when routing to Triton vs CUTLASS. p50 looks fine but p99 jumps ~18% after last deploy.

maria: Which path is taking the hit? Triton only or the fallback hops?

aj: Seems to be when router picks Triton for mixed batches (seq distribution has a fat tail). Logs show more back-and-forth: Triton accepts, then falls back to CUTLASS for a few requests due to reservation timeout.

kai: Can you paste the snippet of the router decision log?

aj: Sure: 
```
[2026-03-18T14:02:10Z] request id=... seq=128 batch=6 chosen=Triton reason=latency_pref
[2026-03-18T14:02:10Z] probe: Triton queue depth spike -> fallback_candidate=true
[2026-03-18T14:02:10Z] fallback action=route_to_cutlass reason=slot_timeout latency_est=1.08ms
```

ben: That looks like a slot contention issue. We changed the slot timeout last week to be more aggressive (to lower average latency), but that can create oscillation for long-seq requests.

maria: Is KV cache warmup impacting it? Long sequences have larger KV working set; if KV is cold, Triton latency can spike due to kernel path choosing different schedule.

aj: Exactly — profiler output for a repro run: 
```
seq=128, batch=6
Triton kernels: matmul_main 1.22ms, kv_load 0.48ms, sync_wait 0.30ms -> total 2.00ms
Cutlass kernels: matmul_main 0.95ms, kv_load 0.35ms -> total 1.45ms
```
We see Triton path higher for this pattern.

kai: Interesting that Cutlass is faster here; probably because Cutlass's matmul kernel uses a different tiling for this shape and avoids an extra synchronization. But the router's cost model predicted Triton would be better for <seq 192 historically.

ben: Two angles: (1) make router include a KV-hotness factor in the cost estimate, (2) make fallback hysteresis less eager for sequences with large KV footprints.

maria: I'd add a probabilistic smoothing: if a route flips more than N times in T seconds for the same request signature, route to the stable candidate (Cutlass) for the next M requests.

aj: I ran an A/B with probabilistic smoothing enabled: p99 dropped ~12% for the tail but p50 unchanged. Sample config diff: 
```
router.smoothing.enabled = true
router.smoothing.window_sec = 30
router.smoothing.flip_threshold = 3
router.smoothing.force_stable_duration = 10
```

perf-bot: Perf test triggered: test-suite/kernel-routing/seq-128-batch-6/stable-smoothing (run id 20260318-09)

kai: Nice. Can we also add a KV-cache-aware probe that increases sampling for requests with large seq to build better latency priors? Right now probe sampling is uniform and undersamples the tail.

ben: Agreed. Proposed probe change: sample_prob = base_prob * max(1, seq/64) clipped at 0.2. That should get us more telemetry without exploding overhead.

maria: Also add a fallback metric: count of 'route flip' events per minute per route signature. We can alert if flips > 10/min.

aj: I'll open a quick PR: add smoothing + probe tweak + flip metric. Also include a short experiment: run canary with smoothing on 10% of traffic for 6 hours.

ben: Add a guard: if smoothing forces Cutlass but Cutlass latency goes above X% of expected, fallback to Triton (so we don't stick with a degraded path).

kai: Sounds solid. After PR, let's run the perf-bot suite and a small canary. If results are good, roll change to 50% and re-evaluate.

maria: Thanks — major action items: aj PR, perf tests, add flip alert, tweak probe sampling.

aj: PR opened: https://git.local/redwood/runtime/pulls/2783 — includes logs, config, and an automated smokecheck.

perf-bot: Canary scheduled: 2026-03-18T18:00:00Z on h100 pool (10% traffic).
